The '''Wakka Wakka''' language, also spelt '''Waga''', or '''Wakawaka''', is an extinct [[Pama–Nyungan]] language formerly spoken by the [[Wakka Wakka]] people, an [[Aboriginal Australian]] nation near [[Brisbane]], Australia.<ref>[http://www.atsida.edu.au/archive/language-groups/waka-waka Waka Waka] - ATSIDA</ref> Kaiabara/Gayabara, Nguwera/Ngoera, and Buyibara may be varieties or alternative names.

== Initiation language ==
A distinct style of the language was used in male initiation ceremonies. Two phrases or words were given by an unitiated informant with unknown meaning., being {{Lang|wkw|biri buːn barung}} and {{Lang|wkw|marugung}}.{{Sfn|Kite|Wurm|2004|p=9}}
